title: How the age rating for series works
seoTitle: How the age rating for series works
subtitle: Find out who decides, what the criteria are, and how it affects the audience
excerpt: The age rating guides parents and viewers about series content, defining age brackets and explaining the criteria used by reviewers.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The age rating guides series viewers on content suitability for different age groups. It emerges as a tool for protecting minors and informing the general public. Understand how the process works and what it means for those who produce and consume television entertainment.

Who determines the age rating

The responsibility falls on a governmental body specialized in audiovisual content assessment. This body brings together professionals from fields such as psychology, sociology, and communication, who analyze each work independently. The decision is made based on established criteria, aiming to balance creative freedom and protection of vulnerable audiences.

Evaluators work in regular sessions, where each episode or season undergoes a detailed analysis. During this process, the creators' intentions, narrative context, and the way sensitive elements are presented are considered. The final result is recorded in a report that serves as the basis for assigning the rating.

Criteria used in the evaluation

To assign a rating, evaluators consider four main pillars that cover different dimensions of audiovisual content.

  • Violence: presence of aggression scenes, their intensity and context. The number of blows, severity of injuries, and whether there is narrative justification are observed.
  • Sexuality: exposure of intimate acts, suggestive language, and representations of relationships. The level of explicitness, presence of nudity, and how the theme is handled are assessed.
  • Language: use of profanity, offensive terms, or aggressive slang. The frequency of expressions and their potential to offend are analyzed.
  • Sensitive topics: coverage of drugs, alcohol, discrimination, or risky situations. The focus is on how these subjects are presented and whether there is a risk of glamorization.

Each pillar is examined for frequency, level of explicitness, and potential impact on the viewer. The combination of these factors determines the recommended age bracket. When content presents multiple critical elements, the evaluator may weigh the severity of each to reach a balanced decision.

Age brackets and their meanings

The categories vary according to the expected maturity of the audience. The main ratings are structured to provide clarity to the viewer.

  • All audiences: content deemed suitable for children and adults, without elements that could cause discomfort.
  • 12 years: caregivers' attention is recommended for themes that may upset preteens, such as mild violence or moderate language.
  • 14 years: indicates presence of violence or stronger language, still within acceptable limits for teenagers, as well as possible references to romantic relationships.
  • 16 years: signals content that may contain explicit sexual scenes or harsher violence, requiring greater maturity to comprehend.
  • 18 years: reserved for material that exceeds tolerance limits for minors, such as extreme violence, explicit sexuality, or highly controversial topics.

Each badge appears before the series starts and accompanies the descriptions on digital platforms, providing the audience with a clear reference. The presence of a specific badge also guides content providers to adjust distribution and promotion strategies.

How the rating appears on platforms

On streaming services, cable TV channels, and video-on-demand platforms, the rating is displayed in a standardized way. Typically, the badge appears near the title, accompanied by an icon indicating the age bracket. In some cases, there is also a summary of the reasons behind that rating, allowing the viewer to quickly understand the relevant aspects.

When a user attempts to access content rated above their age bracket, the platform may request confirmation from a guardian or block access, depending on internal policies. This barrier works as a parental control mechanism, which can be configured according to each family's preferences.

In addition to direct viewing, platforms usually offer search filters that allow users to select only content within a specific age bracket. This feature facilitates programming curation for schools, institutions, and family environments.

Impacts on consumption and production

For the audience, the rating facilitates conscious choices, avoiding uncomfortable or inappropriate situations. Parents and guardians can filter what is shown in family settings, while adults have the freedom to decide according to their preferences. The badge also serves as an indicator of thematic quality, helping viewers align expectations.

For producers, the rating indicates limits to be observed during script creation. Knowing the criteria allows planning the narrative to reach the desired age bracket, impacting budget, casting, and marketing strategy decisions. When the goal is to reach a broader audience, creators tend to modulate scenes of violence or sexuality to keep the rating at lower levels.

Moreover, the rating can influence international distribution, as many regions adopt similar systems. A series well-rated in one country may have its rating adjusted when exported, requiring adaptations or cuts to meet different regulations. This flexibility expands the reach of Brazilian productions while ensuring respect for the sensitivities of diverse audiences.

In summary, the age rating functions as a guide that balances artistic freedom and social responsibility, ensuring that the audience chooses what to watch with sufficient information. Understanding this process helps both producers and consumers, making the world of series more transparent and safe.
